Why do people waste so much time at the office?

Because they can get away with it. Besides, before wasting time on the Internet was fashionable, people wasted time talking to each other in the office.

People are generally only maximally productive for bouts of about 2 hours at a time.

Precisely. It is a very rare day for me to even be capable of 9 hours of sustained work on tasks (I do largely mental, office kind of work). You simply cannot concentrate for that long, day in, day out.

I really only work about 2-3 hours a day. The rest is talking to co-workers, internet, or nonsense meetings. Our productivity is unbelievable compared to past years, but we are still required to show up and 'be available'.

I can't help but think of all the things I could be doing instead of wasting hours at work. I am somewhat hopeful that it will change before I retire, but not betting on it.
Why would you want it changed? Would you be fine only being payed 3 hours a day, versus the 8 for 3 currently?

I would prefer to be paid based on results rather than social availability. I didn't mention it but a large part of my time is also waiting on other people. There is also no reason I shouldn't be telecommuting nearly full time for my work.

Frankly it would be better for me to have multiple jobs working a handful of hours on each, but that would be pretty hard for me to do at this stage.

Yeah that would be ideal for me as well. Well here's to hoping newer businesses adopt new methods.

I know that many in the cryptocurrency space envision decentralized autonomous corporations where people are payed by their work (bounties): http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralized_Autonomous_Organization#Decentralized_Autonomous_Corporations.2FCompanies_.28DACs.29

I suppose it depends on the country, but the American system or approach to work is just extremely unhealthy. I can think of a few occasions where I've brought up the amount of holiday time in Europe to friends who work in offices and they have almost an antagonistic response to it. I can think of at least several friends that fail to discern between themselves and their given occupation.

I've seen this myself. Sometimes a person can be very career driven and identify with their work, but I haven't found most people to be like that.

The antagonistic response is something I've never been able to figure out. If a person hears an industry (government for instance) offers a large amount of paid time off, they ask 'why do they get this' instead of 'why don't I get this'.

Yes, vacation time and a pension are where I most often hear the sentiment. Like you noted, I don't think its overly prevalent. I think most people are content to show and put in the work they feel necessary...I guess I'd estimate that maybe 30% of my friends have what I would consider an "unhealthy" work-life balance. Not that there's anything wrong with that.
